sources.entry: SeaweedFS | Distributed file system to store and serve billions of files fast

summary.one_liner: SeaweedFS is a distributed file system and blob store, written in Go, designed to store billions of files and serve them quickly, with optional filer, S3, WebDAV and FUSE mount layers.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a master server that manages volumes, volume servers that hold blob data and per-file metadata, and an optional stateless Filer that adds directories and POSIX-style attributes on top of pluggable metadata stores (MySQL, Postgres, Redis, Cassandra, LevelDB, RocksDB, SQLite, etcd and others). Files can be read and written over HTTP, through an S3-compatible API, via WebDAV, or mounted as a local directory with FUSE. It supports replication with rack and data center awareness, automatic master failover, TTL expiration, compaction, and erasure coding for warm data. It can also tier older volumes to cloud object storage and asynchronously replicate between clusters. A "weed mini" command starts master, volume, filer, S3, WebDAV and admin UI in one process for single-node use, while "weed server" is the production-oriented setup.
use_cases: shared network drive via FUSE or WebDAV
how_to_run: Download the weed binary, then run: ./weed mini -dir=/data
notable: Filer metadata can live in many existing databases such as MySQL, Postgres, Redis, Cassandra and etcd
O(1) disk read for file access, with about 16 bytes of in-memory metadata per blob
Tiered storage that offloads warm volumes to cloud object storage
weed mini auto-configures a complete single-host setup with one command
Rack- and data center-aware replication settings
caveats: Some features, such as custom EC ratios and a self-healing storage format, are only in the Enterprise Edition, which the README points to seaweedfs.com for
The README's own benchmarks are described as unscientific single-machine results
The Installation Guide notes that building from source requires Go and a configured GOPATH
